chunks: Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Whoever guarantees a trader has nothing but the principal capital, and he has no share at all in the profit.”

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.تَاجِرًا: a trader engaged in commercial activity
key_terms.رَأْسُ الْمَالِ: the principal amount of capital originally invested or owed
key_terms.ضَمَّنَ: guaranteed or assumed liability for another party

ai.seo_question: If someone guarantees a trader, are they entitled to any share of the profit?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning a person who guarantees a trader. Such a person is entitled only to the original capital and is not entitled to any portion of the profit, indicating a distinction between guarantee and profit-sharing in financial dealings.
